Hello neighbors, this is Cascade Legal Rights Project. Thank you to the moderator for inviting us to respond, and thank you to everyone who spoke up. Getting a letter from a law firm right after asking for help is scary, and we understand why people are worried and want answers.

Here is how we handle the information people share with us at the clinic:

- Our policy prohibits giving attendee information to landlords or their attorneys.
- It also prohibits sharing, selling, or disclosing that information for any purpose.
- Sign-in records stay with our organization and are kept in locked storage.

On the letters, eviction cases filed in Magistrate Court are public records. Some law firms and other businesses look through those filings and mail people whose names appear on them. That is the most likely explanation for letters like the ones described here. A person can get one whether or not they ever came to a clinic. We won't discuss anyone's individual situation in a public thread, because the privacy of the people we serve matters to us.

The clinic is still happening this Saturday, November 14, from 10am to 1pm, and everyone is welcome. One change: the library meeting room is closed that day for repairs, so we are moving to the Mt Zion Fellowship Hall in East Atlanta. Use the side entrance by the parking lot, which is accessible. Volunteer attorneys and staff will be there to look over eviction notices and court papers and talk through your options. No appointment is needed.

If you have questions about how we handle information, or anything else about the clinic, please email clinic@cascaderights.example or call our office at 404-555-0187. We would rather you ask us directly than go without help because you're unsure.

Thank you for caring about your neighbors.

Cascade Legal Rights Project
